podcast.title: Underwhelming Post-Creed Project
podcast.body: This group, formed by the former bandmates of Scott Stapp after Creed, was described as "underwhelming." "Their post-crede group is called Alter Bridge. And well, underwhelming, you know."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: "The Woman with the Golden Ears" in A&R
xref.body: Meltzer transitioned into A&R, where she gained a reputation as "The Woman with the Golden Ears" due to her exceptional ability to identify and sign hit acts. Her keen ear led her to sign prominent bands such as Creed, Evanescence, Alter Bridge, Finger 11, Drowning Pool, and Bright Eyes. "And because she was so good at picking hit acts, she became known as the Woman with the Golden Ears."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Breakup Project (Alter Bridge)
xref.body: After Creed, Scott Stapp's former bandmates formed a new group called Alter Bridge. "Their post-crede group is called Alter Bridge."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Shared "Guitarist First" Affliction with Ian Thorneley
xref.body: Miles Kennedy, known for singing with Slash and Alter Bridge, shares a long-standing history with Ian Thorneley and a common trait of primarily identifying as a guitarist rather than a singer, though Kennedy has since adapted to the frontman role without a guitar. "Oddly enough, like Miles, who sings with slash all the time, the, the mild and I go way back and, and we suffer from the same affliction where guitar players first and singers second."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Shared "Guitarist First" Affliction with Miles Kennedy
xref.body: Ian Thorneley notes a long-standing connection with Miles Kennedy, lead singer for Slash's solo band and Alter Bridge. They share the characteristic of being "guitar players first and singers second," although Kennedy has since embraced the frontman role without a guitar. "Oddly enough, like Miles, who sings with slash all the time, the, the mild and I go way back and, and we suffer from the same affliction where guitar players first and singers second."
